sentences.english_text: Chapter 11, Drippy had no idea where he was.
One moment he was on the stage in front of a huge audience and the next moment the stage and the audience had disappeared.
Or at least it seemed that way to Drippy.
What had actually happened, of course, was that Drippy had disappeared.
The table that the magician had put the rabbit on was directly over a trap door that went down to the basement.
And when the magician had covered the cage with a cloth, the trap door was open so that the cage, the rabbit and Drippy dropped down to the basement.
It was dark down there and Drippy said, I've got to get out of here.
He crawled out of the rabbit's ear and started upstairs.
Applause On the stage, meanwhile, the show was coming to an end.
Mr. Harris, the magician, took his bows and the audience got up and started to leave the theater.
The wind had had a meeting with the mouse and the cricket and the bluebird.
As soon as the doors open, I'll go in and search for Drippy.
And you all keep an eye open for him in case I miss him.
And that is the way it was arranged.
So now, when the ushers opened the doors to let the people out, the wind whistled inside and went up to the stage where he had been told Drippy was.
The wind looked everywhere, but Drippy was nowhere to be seen.
The mouse crouched in his corner, watching carefully to see if Drippy passed by.
No Drippy.
The cricket stood by the stage door to see if he could find Drippy.
There was no sign of Drippy.
Outside the theater, the bluebird watched the people coming out.
But there was no Drippy.
The wind said, He must be in here somewhere.
We'll just wait until we find him.
And they probably would have found him, except that fate stepped in.
And they probably would have found him, except that fate stepped in.
